column1: Coach Marv explains sport by drawing circles on it. Once he circled the sun. Ten minutes, skapi.
column2: Coach Marv explains sport by drawin circles on it. Once he circled the sun. Ten minutes, skapi.

column1: Tonight: test patterns, the video synth, and drawing on the picture. Press START.
column2: The nicht: test patterns, the video synth, an drawin on the picture. Press START.

column1: Get me a picture and a pen. BOOM.
column2: Get me a picture an a pen. BOOM.

column1: Line up the screens BEFORE the show. Not during. I learned this in Plovdiv.
column2: Line up the screens BEFORE the show. Not durin. I learned this in Plovdiv.

column1: Every desk needs a test pattern. PATTERN adds Pocket Test: checked against real meters.
column2: Every desk needs a test pattern. TEST CAIRD adds Pocket Test: checked against real meters.

column1: My favourite. SOURCE, then Video Synth: oscillators, mirrors and feedback. No camera needed.
column2: Ma favourite. SOURCE, then Video Synth: oscillators, mirrors an feedback. Nae camera needed.

column1: Now here's a replay. And here's a guy. And BOOM, he's in it.
column2: Noo here's a replay. And here's a guy. And BOOM, he's in it.

column1: Ink goes on top, on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Ink goes on top, on its ain layer. Press the + at the end o the playlist tabs.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the first. Like a second oscillator, mixed on top.
column2: A second playlist is a layer ower the first. Like a second oscillator, mixed on top.

column1: In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Draw. Clear everywhere you have not drawn.
column2: In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Draw. Clear everywhere ye have no drawn.

column1: Select the Draw cue and TAKE it. Two playlists, two layers, one picture.
column2: Select the Draw cue an TAKE it. Twa playlists, twa layers, wan picture.

column1: Now both are live: the synth underneath, the ink on top.
column2: Noo both are live: the synth underneath, the ink on top.

column1: Press DRAW in the inspector, then draw on the programme monitor. Mouse, or a pen if you have one.
column2: Press DRAW in the inspector, then draw on the programme monitor. Mouse, or a pen if ye have wan.

column1: A pen's pressure makes the line thicker. A mouse presses at one strength. Like me.
column2: A pen's pressure makes the line thicker. A mouse presses at wan strength. Like me.

column1: Circle him! No, bigger. BOOM. That's a cloud. Fine. Circle the cloud.
column2: Circle him! Nae, bigger. BOOM. That's a cloud. Fine. Circle the cloud.

column1: SAVE STILL keeps the drawing as a picture with a clear background, and adds it to the playlist.
column2: SAVE STILL keeps the drawin as a picture wi a clear background, an adds it tae the playlist.

column1: Try Replay in the Draw section: it draws your lines back the way you drew them.
column2: Try Replay in the Draw section: it draws yer lines back the way ye drew them.

column1: Same time next week. Bring a bigger pen. And a turducken.
column2: Same time next week. Bring a bigger pen. An a haggis.

column1: The Bureau of Unexplained Signals. Two agents, one photo, and it must not air. Press START.
column2: The Bureau o Unexplained Signals. Twa agents, wan photo, an it must no air. Press START.

column1: Masks cut a picture into shapes. Tonight we cut evidence.
column2: Masks cut a picture into shapes. The nicht we cut evidence.

column1: That's a craft, Brandt. Look at the lights. I want to believe.
column2: That's a craft, Brandt. Look at the lights. I want tae believe.

column1: In the inspector's MASK section: mask, then 'new heart'. Any shape will do. The heart is funnier.
column2: In the inspector's MASK section: mask, then 'new heart'. Any shape will dae. The heart is funnier.

column1: The library has circles, stars, hearts. Each one is points you can move.
column2: The library has circles, stars, hearts. Each wan is points ye can move.

column1: A heart, Hollis? The Bureau redacts with black bars.
column2: A heart, Hollis? The Bureau redacts wi black bars.

column1: Set the tool to pen, then click round the saucer on the monitor. Click the first point to close it.
column2: Set the tool tae pen, then click round the saucer on the monitor. Click the first point tae close it.

column1: Draw round it carefully. It might be watching.
column2: Draw round it carefully. It might be watchin.

column1: Invert keeps the outside and cuts the inside. The saucer goes. The sky stays.
column2: Invert keeps the outside an cuts the inside. The saucer goes. The sky stays.

column1: The same shape, the other way round. Very useful. Slightly spooky.
column2: The same shape, the other way round. Awfy useful. Slightly spooky.

column1: A hard edge says 'someone was here'. A soft one says nothing at all.
column2: A hard edge says 'someone was here'. A soft wan says naethin at aw.

column1: A library shape, the pen, invert and feather. The Bureau thanks you. The Bureau was never here.
column2: A library shape, the pen, invert an feather. The Bureau thanks ye. The Bureau was never here.

column1: A lighthouse, a ghost, and a keeper who has been alone with the lamp far too long. Press START.
column2: A lighthouse, a ghost, an a keeper wha has been alone wi the lamp far tae long. Press START.

column1: Projection mapping: bending the picture to fit the building. Warp, blend, slices.
column2: Projection mapping: bendin the picture tae fit the buildin. Warp, blend, slices.

column1: Ye'll be wanting the ghost on the windows. Mind the lamp. The lamp is MINE.
column2: Ye'll be wantin the ghaist on the windaes, aye? Mind the lamp. The lamp is MINE. Haud yer wheesht aboot it.

column1: MENU, then Video Outputs, then Geometry. Where an output's shape lives.
column2: MENU, then Video ootpits, then Geometry. Whaur an output's shape lives.

column1: Press warp edit, then drag a corner on the programme monitor. The window is not square. Neither is the keeper.
column2: Press warp edit, then drag a corner on the programme monitor. The window is no square. Neither is the keeper.

column1: Back in Geometry: edge blend, + on the left and + on the right.
column2: Back in Geometry: edge blend, + on the left an + on the richt.

column1: Two projectors overlap; each fades its edge so the overlap is not twice as bright.
column2: Twa projectors overlap; each fades its edge so the overlap is no twice as bright.

column1: Geometry, SLICES, open. The Screens window is where slices are cut and placed.
column2: Geometry, SLICES, open. The Screens window is whaur slices are cut an placed.

column1: A slice is a piece of the picture, put anywhere on the output.
column2: A slice is a piece o the picture, put anywhere on the output.

column1: In the Screens window, + SLICE three times, and drag each crop to a third of the picture.
column2: In the Screens window, + SLICE three times, an drag each crop tae a third o the picture.

column1: Three windows, three slices: left, middle and right of one picture.
column2: Three windows, three slices: left, middle an richt o wan picture.

column1: Three windows. The lamp gets the middle one. The lamp ALWAYS gets the middle one.
column2: Three windows. The lamp gets the middle wan. The lamp ALWAYS gets the middle wan.

column1: Warp, blend, slices. The keeper will finally sleep. The gulls will not.
column2: Warp, blend, slices. The keeper will finally sleep. The gulls will no.

column1: Slices have their own warp and mesh in the Screens window. And a ~ on the place and the turn.
column2: Slices have their ain warp an mesh in the Screens window. And a ~ on the place an the turn.

column1: Ye did alright, lad. Now get away from the lamp.
column2: Ye did alright, laddie. Noo get away fae the lamp.

column1: A game show, skapi. Three contestants, one buzzer, and cues that fire from anywhere. Press START.
column2: A game show, skapi. Three contestants, wan buzzer, an cues that fire fae anywhere. Press START.

column1: Cue numbers, hotkeys, and GO from other machines. Like a sequencer you can play from any key.
column2: Cue numbers, hotkeys, an GO fae other machines. Like a sequencer ye can play fae ony key.

column1: Welcome to the show! Let's spin that wheel!
column2: Welcome tae the show! Gie that wheel a birl!

column1: Theatre numbers its cues. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Deckboy reads them all.
column2: Theatre numbers its cues. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Deckboy reads them aw.

column1: I'd like to buy a number, please.
column2: I'd like tae buy a number, please.

column1: Ctrl+G, type the number, Enter. It goes live wherever the list happens to be standing.
column2: Ctrl+G, type the number, Enter. It goes live wherever the list happens tae be standin.

column1: GOTO. The fastest way across a long list. Faster than scrolling. Much faster than me.
column2: GOTO. The fastest way across a long list. Faster than scrollin. Much faster than me.

column1: Contestant 1 is selected. In TRIGGERS, press key, then F5. That key now fires this cue.
column2: Contestant 1 is selected. In TRIGGERS, press key, then F5. That key noo fires this cue.

column1: F1 to F10, F12, or the number pad. Each one, a buzzer.
column2: F1 tae F10, F12, or the number pad. Each wan, a buzzer.

column1: Press the key. The cue fires, wherever the list is standing.
column2: Press the key. The cue fires, wherever the list is standin.

column1: No mouse, no list, no looking. Just the key.
column2: Nae mouse, nae list, nae lookin. Just the key.

column1: Companion, a MIDI note, an OSC message: MENU, then Network, says where each one connects.
column2: Companion, a MIDI note, an OSC message: MENU, then Network, says whaur each wan connects.

column1: And for our viewers at home: you can play along too.
column2: And for our viewers at hame: ye can play along tae.

column1: Numbers, GOTO, a buzzer, and GO from anywhere. You are a game show now, skapi.
column2: Numbers, GOTO, a buzzer, an GO fae anywhere. Ye are a game show noo, skapi.

column1: A cue can have a key, a MIDI note and an OSC address at once. Belt, braces and a second belt.
column2: A cue can have a key, a MIDI note an an OSC address at once. Belt, braces an a second belt.

column1: Channel 6 weather, skapi. A map, a presenter, and a very large lizard. Press START.
column2: Channel 6 weather, skapi. A map, a presenter, an an awfy muckle lizard. Fower seasons in wan day, an a lizard. Press START.

column1: Words on screen: Lower Thirds, text, and backdrops.
column2: Words on screen: Lower Thirds, text, an backdrops.

column1: I'm June O'Neil, and nothing about this forecast is normal.
column2: I'm June O'Neil, an naethin aboot this forecast is normal.

column1: Words go on their own layer: press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Words go on their ain layer: press the + at the end o the playlist tabs.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the map. The lizard stays underneath. Mostly.
column2: A second playlist is a layer ower the map. The lizard stays underneath. Mostly.

column1: A name and a title, low on the screen, out of the lizard's way.
column2: A name an a title, low on the screen, oot o the lizard's way.

column1: Spelling counts. The audience reads it at the speed of light.
column2: Spellin counts. The audience reads it at the speed o licht.

column1: Spell it right. Last week it said 'Jane O'Meal'.
column2: Spell it richt. Last week it said 'June O'Neep'.

column1: TAKE the Lower Third. Her name slides in over the map.
column2: TAKE the Lower Third. Her name slides in ower the map.

column1: Two layers live: the weather, and the words on top of it.
column2: Twa layers live: the weather, an the words on top o it.

column1: Thank you. Now, about that lizard...
column2: Thank ye. Noo, aboot that lizard...

column1: SOURCE, then Text: a title card. Then its backdrop chip: key green, for the vision mixer to key out.
column2: SOURCE, then Text: a title card. Then its backdrop chip: key green, for the vision mixer tae key oot.

column1: A backdrop fills behind the words. Key green or key blue, and the mixer does the rest.
column2: A backdrop fills behind the words. Key green or key blue, an the mixer dis the rest.

column1: Breaking news: it's standing on the five-day forecast.
column2: Breakin news: it's standin on the five-day forecast.

column1: Lower Thirds can wait, slide and leave on their own. Their section has every setting.
column2: Lower Thirds can wait, slide an leave on their ain. Their section has every settin.

column1: That's the weather. Back to you, guys. Run.
column2: That's the weather. Back tae the studio. Rin. Tak a jaiket.

column1: A rocket built in a basement, skapi, and an inventor who wants cheese. Press START.
column2: A rocket built in a basement, skapi, an an inventor wha wants cheese. Press START.

column1: Stage timers: countdowns, clocks, and a presenter view for the person on stage.
column2: Stage timers: countdowns, clocks, an a presenter view for the person on stage.

column1: SOURCE, then Stage Timer. A clock that counts down, in big friendly numbers.
column2: SOURCE, then Stage Timer. A clock that counts doon, in big friendly numbers.

column1: Its colours change as it runs out: white, amber, red. Like a VU meter for time.
column2: Its colours change as it runs oot: white, amber, red. Like a VU meter for time.

column1: Select the timer and TAKE it. The countdown starts.
column2: Select the timer an TAKE it. The countdown starts.

column1: Past zero it keeps going, counting the overtime. Very honest. Slightly rude.
column2: Past zero it keeps gaun, countin the overtime. Awfy honest. Slightly rude.

column1: Ten... nine... ooh, I do love a countdown.
column2: Ten... nine... ooh, I dae love a countdown.

column1: Something's loose! Space holds the countdown. The clock shows it is held.
column2: Somethin's loose! Space holds the countdown. The clock shows it is held.

column1: A hold is not a stop. Space again, and it carries on from where it was.
column2: A hold is no a stop. Space again, an it carries on fae whaur it was.

column1: MENU, Video Outputs: make an output's type PRESENTER. The person on stage gets the timer, the next cue and their notes.
column2: MENU, Video ootpits: make an output's type PRESENTER. The person on stage gets the timer, the next cue an their notes.

column1: A presenter view is an output like any other. Point it at the confidence monitor.
column2: A presenter view is an output like ony other. Point it at the confidence monitor.

column1: A countdown, a hold, and a view for the pilot. Nazdrave, skapi. Bring crackers.
column2: A countdown, a hold, an a view for the pilot. Nazdrave, skapi. Brin crackers.

column1: Timers can also count up, or show the time of day. Their section has the lot.
column2: Timers can also count up, or show the time o day. Their section has the lot.

column1: A grand day out, Grommet! Pass the crackers.
column2: A grand day oot, Grommet! Pass the crackers.

column1: A magic show, skapi. A trunk, a prop, and one beat where everything changes at once. Press START.
column2: A magic show, skapi. A trunk, a prop, an wan beat whaur awthin changes at once. Press START.

column1: Two playlists are two layers. TAKE ALL changes both together.
column2: Twa playlists are twa layers. TAKE ALL changes both together.

column1: Every trick needs two things happening at once. And a rubber chicken.
column2: Every trick needs twa things happenin at once. And a rubber chicken.

column1: The prop goes on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: The prop goes on its ain layer. Press the + at the end o the playlist tabs.

column1: Playlist 2 sits on top of playlist 1. Like a transparency on an overhead projector.
column2: Playlist 2 sits on top o playlist 1. Like a transparency on an overhead projector.

column1: Nothing up my sleeve. Everything in my trunk.
column2: Naethin up ma sleeve. Awthin in ma trunk.

column1: In the new playlist, add anything: PATTERN will do. That is the prop.
column2: In the new playlist, add onythin: TEST CAIRD will dae. That is the prop.

column1: Select 'The trunk (open)' in playlist 1 and the prop in playlist 2. Then TAKE ALL: both on one beat.
column2: Select 'The trunk (open)' in playlist 1 an the prop in playlist 2. Then TAKE ALL: both on wan beat.

column1: One press, every playlist's selected cue. The audience never sees the seam.
column2: Wan press, every playlist's selected cue. The audience never sees the seam.

column1: Two layers, one beat. Every playlist has its own opacity and can sit on any output. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: Twa layers, wan beat. Every playlist has its ain opacity an can sit on ony output. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A magician never reveals. A playlist never minds being revealed.
column2: A magician never reveals. A playlist never minds bein revealed.

column1: Thank you! I'm here all week! The chicken is here forever.
column2: Ta very much! A'm here aw week! The chookie's here forever.

column1: A cooking show, skapi. Live. Everything is on fire. Press START.
column2: A cookin show, skapi. Live. Awthin is on fire. Press START.

column1: BLACK hides the picture and keeps the show running. PANIC stops everything. Know which you need.
column2: BLACK hides the picture an keeps the show runnin. PANIC stops awthin. Know which ye need.

column1: The audience must not see this. Press BLACK, or B.
column2: The audience must no see this. Press BLACK, or B.

column1: The picture goes. The cue keeps playing underneath, ready to come back.
column2: The picture goes. The cue keeps playin underneath, ready tae come back.

column1: The fire's out. Press B again: the picture comes back, still running.
column2: The fire's oot. Press B again: the picture comes back, still runnin.

column1: Nothing was lost. A mute on a mixer, for pictures.
column2: Naethin was lost. A mute on a mixer, for pictures.

column1: Worse: MENU, System, the SAFETY card: PANIC. Everything stops, the way the panic setting says.
column2: Worse: MENU, System, the SAFETY card: PANIC. Awthin stops, the way the panic settin says.

column1: PANIC is the big red button. Use it when BLACK is not enough. Then breathe.
column2: PANIC is the big red button. Use it when BLACK is no enough. Then breathe.

column1: Close MENU, select the souffle, and TAKE it. The show is back on.
column2: Close MENU, select the souffle, an TAKE it. The show is back on.

column1: After a panic, the show is still there. Pick up where you meant to be.
column2: After a panic, the show is still there. Pick up whaur ye meant tae be.

column1: BLACK to hide, PANIC to stop, TAKE to come back. You will survive any kitchen, skapi.
column2: BLACK tae hide, PANIC tae stop, TAKE tae come back. Ye will survive ony kitchen, skapi.

column1: The panic setting chooses what PANIC does: fade out, cut, or just the outputs.
column2: The panic settin chooses whit PANIC dis: fade oot, cut, or just the outputs.

column1: Presets, skapi. A whole look, remembered, and back with one button. Press START.
column2: Presets, skapi. A whole look, remembered, an back wi wan button. Press START.

column1: Press DASH: buttons of your own, for anything at all.
column2: Press DASH: buttons o yer ain, for onythin at aw.

column1: Ctrl+D also works. Very fast. Very professional.
column2: Ctrl+D also works. Awfy fast. Awfy professional.

column1: Store. Like saving the patch before the drummer leans on the synth.
column2: Store. Like savin the patch afore the drummer leans on the synth.

column1: Close the DASH (Esc), then select Look two and TAKE it. A different look.
column2: Close the DASH (Esc), then select Look twa an TAKE it. A different look.

column1: Change it all. Don't worry. It remembers.
column2: Change it aw. Dinnae worry. It remembers.

column1: Open the DASH and press your preset button. The first look comes back.
column2: Open the DASH an press yer preset button. The first look comes back.

column1: Recall. The patch memory, returning. Beautiful.
column2: Recall. The patch memory, returnin. Beautiful.

column1: A look, stored and recalled. A preset can keep cues, positions, effects, levels and routing; its button's menu chooses which.
column2: A look, stored an recalled. A preset can keep cues, positions, effects, levels an routing; its button's menu chooses which.

column1: And a DASH button can run any command at all. Any. Even the exciting ones.
column2: And a DASH button can run ony command at aw. Any. Even the excitin ones.

column1: A space-opera trailer, skapi. A narrator with a very deep voice and opinions about transitions. Press START.
column2: A space-opera trailer, skapi. A narrator wi a awfy deep voice an opinions aboot transitions. Press START.

column1: A transition is how one cue becomes the next. There are far more than the crossfade.
column2: A transition is how wan cue becomes the next. There are far more than the crossfade.

column1: In a galaxy of content... one operator... must choose a transition.
column2: In a galaxy o content... wan operator... must choose a transition.

column1: Pushes, wipes, iris, dip to white. Even a portal. I wrote half of them. On a Tuesday.
column2: Pushes, wipes, iris, dip tae white. Even a portal. I wrote half o them. On a Tuesday.

column1: Give it a time: + on transition until it says a second or more.
column2: Give it a time: + on chynge until it says a second or more.

column1: No time, no transition. A style needs a duration to do anything at all.
column2: Nae time, nae transition. A style needs a duration tae dae onythin at aw.

column1: The transition belongs to the cue arriving. Each cue chooses its own entrance.
column2: The transition belongs tae the cue arrivin. Each cue chooses its ain entrance.

column1: Now 'The battle': choose shatter, give it a time, and TAKE it.
column2: Noo 'The battle': choose shatter, give it a time, an TAKE it.

column1: Shatter drops the old picture like a pane of glass. Please do not do this at a funeral.
column2: Shatter drops the auld picture like a pane o glass. Please dinnae dae this at a funeral.

column1: A style, a time, and two very dramatic entrances. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: A style, a time, an twa awfy dramatic entrances. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A playlist has a default style too, for every cue that does not choose its own.
column2: A playlist has a default style tae, for every cue that dis no choose its ain.

column1: Coming soon... to a desk near you.
column2: Comin soon... tae a desk near ye.

column1: Two robot DJs, skapi. They do not talk. Their helmets do. Press START.
column2: Twa robot DJs, skapi. They dinnae talk. Their helmets dae. Press START.

column1: Every cue has its own chain of audio effects, and some of them break the sound on purpose.
column2: Every cue has its ain chain o audio effects, an some o them break the sound on purpose.

column1: The beat is selected. In its AUDIO EFFECTS section, + adds one. Try the delay.
column2: The beat is selected. In its AUDIO EFFECTS section, + adds wan. Try the delay.

column1: > ONE MORE TIME. WITH ECHO. ECHO. ECHO.
column2: > WAN MORE TIME. WITH ECHO. ECHO. ECHO.

column1: Add a second: a bend, like crush. It damages the sound the way a broken file would.
column2: Add a second: a bend, like crush. It damages the sound the way a broken file wid.

column1: The bends are my favourite. Like a tape left in the sun. On purpose.
column2: The bends are ma favourite. Like a tape left in the sun. On purpose.

column1: MENU, then Audio: where each playlist's sound goes, and the patch for named outputs.
column2: MENU, then Soond: whaur each playlist's sound goes, an the patch for named outputs.

column1: Speakers, monitors, an in-ear for the drummer. The patch sends each its own.
column2: Speakers, monitors, an in-ear for the drummer. The patch sends each its ain.

column1: An effect, a bend and the patch. The robots approve, skapi. I think. Their faces are helmets.
column2: An effect, a bend an the patch. The robots approve, skapi. I think. Their faces are helmets.

column1: Every audio effect can follow a ~ too, even Motion. Wave at the delay. It's wonderful.
column2: Every audio effect can follow a ~ tae, even Motion. Wave at the delay. It's wonderful.

column1: > THANK YOU. GOOD NIGHT. WE ARE ROBOTS.
column2: > THANK YOU. GOOD NICHT. WE ARE ROBOTS.

column1: The Bureau again, skapi. A glow on the horizon, and two agents who disagree about it. Press START.
column2: The Bureau again, skapi. A glow on the horizon, an twa agents wha disagree aboot it. Press START.

column1: The scopes measure a picture: brightness, colour, levels. Numbers, not opinions.
column2: The scopes measure a picture: brightness, colour, levels. Numbers, no opinions.

column1: The scopes read only what really goes out, never a preview. Turn the output on: MENU, Video Outputs, OUTPUT OFF.
column2: The scopes read only whit really goes oot, never a preview. Turn the output on: MENU, Video ootpits, OOTPIT AFF.

column1: Measuring a scaled-down preview would be measuring a photocopy. We measure the original.
column2: Measurin a scaled-doon preview wid be measurin a photocopy. We measure the original.

column1: Chain of evidence, Hollis. The real signal or nothing.
column2: Chain o evidence, Hollis. The real signal or naethin.

column1: Both shows the picture and its scopes side by side. Very civilised.
column2: Both shows the picture an its scopes side by side. Awfy civilised.

column1: Click the waveform to make it big. Bright things sit high, dark things low, left to right as in the picture.
column2: Click the waveform tae make it big. Bright things sit high, dark things low, left tae richt as in the picture.

column1: The glow is that spike near the top. Very bright. Bright is not the same as alien.
column2: The glow is that spike near the top. Awfy bright. Bright is no the same as alien.

column1: Look at the peak. Nothing a streetlight couldn't do.
column2: Look at the peak. Naethin a streetlight couldnae dae.

column1: Click it again to go back, then click the vectorscope: colour round a circle. Saturated runs to the edge.
column2: Click it again tae go back, then click the vectorscope: colour round a circle. Saturated runs tae the edge.

column1: Magenta, far out by the rim. A strong colour. Strong is not illegal. Yet.
column2: Magenta, far oot by the rim. A strong colour. Strong is no illegal. Yet.

column1: It's off the chart, Brandt! Literally off the chart!
column2: It's aff the chart, Brandt! Literally aff the chart!

column1: Clipped means the brightest the signal can carry, and then some lost. Detail gone.
column2: Clipped means the brightest the signal can carry, an then some lost. Detail gone.

column1: Red. Clipped. Not alien, Hollis. Just too bright. Case closed.
column2: Red. Clipped. Not alien, Hollis. Just tae bright. Case closed.

column1: Waveform, vectorscope, false colour. The scopes settled it, skapi. The agents did not.
column2: Waveform, vectorscope, false colour. The scopes settled it, skapi. The agents did no.

column1: SCOPES SOURCE reads any output, and the matrix can be 709 or 2020. For the curious.
column2: SCOPES SOURCE reads ony output, an the matrix can be 709 or 2020. For the curious.

column1: Too bright for a streetlight, Brandt. Too bright for anything. ...I want to believe.

column2: Scope shaws shape an clippin. Lissajous shaws phase an polarity atween the first twa channels -- a diagonal the wrang wey means ane is inverted. Spectrum is third-octave baurs.

column1: 0 picks the glyph the brightness asks for, 1 picks any glyph in the set. Turn it up to see the whole alphabet: ranked strictly by ink, a flat area picks one mark and the rest never appear.
column2: 0 wales the glyph the brichtness asks for, 1 wales ony glyph in the set. Turn it up tae see the hale alphabet: rankit strictly by ink, a flat area wales ae merk an the lave never shaw.

column1: Blocks and dithers read as density; the ASCII ramp reads as text; symbols read as wreckage. Cycling this clears a custom glyph string, since that would override it -- the preset row puts one back.
column2: Blocks an dithers read as density; the ASCII ramp reads as text; symbols read as wrack. Cyclin this clears a custom glyph string, as that wad owerride it -- the preset raw pits ane back.

column1: Equal temperament buys free modulation at the cost of every interval being slightly wrong. Just and pythagorean are exactly in tune in one key. Bohlen-Pierce divides a twelfth, so it has no octaves.
column2: Equal temperament buys free modulation at the cost o ilka interval bein a wee bit wrang. Just an pythagorean are exactly in tune in ae key. Bohlen-Pierce divides a twalt, sae it haes nae octaves.
